credentialSubject.claim: I will change the LOFL protocol only by publishing a new version that supersedes the old one, and never edit a published version.

selfDeliberation.position: People will build tools on this protocol. If I quietly change a version they rely on, their records break and they cannot trust any LOFL record again. And the protocol's own rule is: nothing is deleted, corrections supersede. If I do not keep that rule for the protocol itself, I cannot ask anyone else to keep it.
selfDeliberation.evidence: Every file has a sha256 in ledger.json, and tools/hash.py --check shows any change. CHANGELOG.md and CONTRIBUTING.md already say: supersede, never edit. I already work this way in my vault, with dated notes and supersession instead of rewrites.
selfDeliberation.counter: A new version for every typo is heavy: readers may face many tiny versions, and a small fix could take days. And v0.1 is a draft no one outside has read. Freezing it now may lock in mistakes that a quiet fix would have caught.
selfDeliberation.consensus: Small fixes wait and go out together in the next version. Nothing published is ever edited, even for a typo.
selfDeliberation.dissent: I am the only steward until the charter's trigger fires. If I break this promise, no one but readers of the git history would notice; no witness is asked yet. And a force-push can rewrite git history. The ledger hashes help, but until the records are anchored somewhere I do not control, 'never edited' rests partly on trust.
